sections.title: NORTH CENTRAL PLAINS/CORN BELT
sections.text: A STRONG CAP/WARM TEMPERATURES ALOFT SHOULD CONFINE DEEP CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT TO ALONG/NORTH OF THE PRIMARY ROUGHLY WNW-ESE FRONTAL BOUNDARY/WARM FRONT ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS/MO RIVER VALLEY. AS A SHORTWAVE TROUGH EMANATING FROM THE SOUTHWEST/ROCKIES ROUNDS THE UPPER RIDGE AND HEIGHTS BEGIN TO FALL ACROSS THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS...STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS SHOULD INITIALLY DEVELOP ACROSS EASTERN WY/FAR NORTHEAST CO AND ADJACENT PORTIONS OF WESTERN NEB BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON...WITH ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT THROUGH LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING ACROSS CENTRAL/EASTERN NEB. MODERATE TO STRONG POTENTIAL INSTABILITY/STEEP LAPSE RATES AND STRENGTHENING MID LEVEL FLOW /40+ KT/...ALONG WITH VEERING WIND PROFILES...WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL /POTENTIALLY SIGNIFICANT/ AND A FEW TORNADOES. ISOLATED TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE AS FAR NORTH AS PORTIONS OF MN/PERHAPS THE FAR EASTERN DAKOTAS WITH AFTERNOON DEVELOPMENT ALONG A WEAK WIND SHIFT. OTHERWISE...AIDED BY THE POTENTIAL MID LEVEL IMPULSE...AND A NOCTURNALLY INCREASING SOUTH-SOUTHWESTERLY LOW LEVEL JET...STORMS MAY CONSOLIDATE/GROW UPSCALE INTO ONE OR MORE MCS/S ACROSS THE EASTERN HALF OF NEB INTO WESTERN IA TONIGHT...POTENTIALL

sections.title: NEB/KS/IA/MO
sections.text: A LARGE UPPER RIDGE IS IN PLACE ACROSS THE SOUTHERN STATES TODAY...WITH BAND OF STRONG MID LEVEL WINDS EXTENDING FROM THE CENTRAL ROCKIES INTO THE MID/UPPER MS VALLEY...THEN EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD TO THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS. MODELS AGREE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SURFACE LOW BY THIS AFTERNOON OVER WESTERN KS WITH BACKED LOW LEVEL WINDS EXPECTED TO THE NORTH OF THE LOW ACROSS MUCH OF NEB. A HOT AND VERY MOIST AIRMASS WILL DEVELOP ACROSS THIS REGION WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S AND TEMPERATURES IN THE 90S. MODEL FORECAST SOUNDINGS ACROSS NEB THIS AFTERNOON SHOW STEEP LOW AND MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND MLCAPE VALUES OF 4500+ J/KG. IT APPEARS LIKELY THAT A COMBINATION OF DIURNAL HEATING AND WEAK LARGE SCALE ASCENT BENEATH THE UPPER JET WILL WEAKEN THE CAP AND LEAD TO SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON FROM EXTREME NORTHEAST CO INTO WESTERN AND CENTRAL NEB. THE INITIAL STORMS WILL LIKELY BE SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF VERY LARGE HAIL AND A FEW TORNADOES. THIS ACTIVITY WILL TRACK EASTWARD ACROSS NEB DURING THE EVENING AND IS EXPECTED TO COALESCE INTO A FAST-MOVING MCS AS STORMS SPREAD INTO IA/KS/MO. THE POTENTIAL EXISTS FOR WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WINDS FROM THIS CLUSTER OF STORMS AC

sections.title: MN/NORTHERN IA
sections.text: REMNANT WEAK UPPER LOW OVER ND WILL LIFT NORTHEASTWARD INTO SOUTHERN CANADA TODAY...WHILE THE SURFACE LOW/TROF BECOMES ESTABLISHED ALONG THE DAKOTA/MN BORDER. SOUTHERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS TO THE EAST OF THE TROF COMBINED WITH VEERING/INCREASING WINDS WITH HEIGHT WILL PROVIDE CONSIDERABLE VERTICAL SHEAR FOR A RISK OF A FEW SUPERCELLS THIS AFTERNOON. AMBIENT LOW LEVEL VORTICITY AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL ALSO AID IN THE RISK OF ISOLATED TORNADOES...ALONG WITH HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. THIS THREAT SHOULD DIMINISH SHORTLY AFTER SUNSET.

sections.title: IA/PA/WV/KY
sections.text: MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SHOWS A STRONG MID LEVEL JET MAX MOVING ACROSS IL. THIS FEATURE WILL TRACK INTO THE UPPER OH VALLEY BY THIS AFTERNOON PROVIDING LARGE SCALE ASCENT AND AIDING IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS. AMPLE MOISTURE/INSTABILITY WILL BE IN PLACE ACROSS MUCH OF OH...WITH A RATHER STRONG THETA-E GRADIENT ACROSS WESTERN PA INTO WV. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW SUFFICIENT VERTICAL SHEAR FOR A RISK OF ORGANIZED MULTICELL AND SCATTERED SUPERCELL STORMS THIS AFTERNOON CAPABLE OF TORNADOES...LARGE HAIL...AND DAMAGING WINDS. EASTWARD PROGRESS INTO CENTRAL PA AND EASTERN WV WILL BE LIMITED BY WEAKER INSTABILITY IN THIS REGION.

sections.title: SOUTHEAST STATES
sections.text: RATHER STRONG NORTHWEST FLOW ALOFT IS PRESENT TODAY OVER THE SOUTHEAST STATES. SCATTERED CLOUDS THIS MORNING WILL GIVE WAY TO POCKETS OF STRONG HEATING THIS AFTERNOON...YIELDING MLCAPE VALUES OVER 2000 J/KG IN MANY AREAS. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO INTENSIFY OVER MUCH OF THE REGION BY MID AFTERNOON AS CONVECTIVE TEMPERATURE IS REACHED AND INITIATION OCCURS OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN. STORMS WILL TRACK SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE RISK AREA WITH A THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SHOWS MULTIPLE WEAK UPPER VORTICITY MAXIMA WHICH MAY HELP TO FOCUS STORMS ACROSS THE REGION.

sections.title: WEST TX
sections.text: HOT CONDITIONS ARE EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON OVER WEST TX WITH TEMPERATURES OVER 100F AND LARGE SURFACE T-TD SPREADS. MODEL GUIDANCE IS IN GOOD AGREEMENT IN DEVELOPING SCATTERED HIGH-BASED SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ALONG AN AXIS FROM SOUTHWEST TX INTO THE SOUTHERN PANHANDLE. INVERTED-V PROFILES AND SUFFICIENT CAPE WILL PROMOTE A RISK OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS IN THE STRONGEST CORES. ..HART/JEWELL.. 06/17/2009

sections.title: NEB/NRN KS/IA/MO
sections.text: WITH UPPER TROUGH IN THE WEST AND RIDGE IN THE SOUTH CENTRAL STATES...A BAND OF STRONGER MID LEVEL WINDS...35 TO 50 KT...EXTENDED ACROSS THE REGION. WEAK SURFACE LOW WAS LOCATED WEST OF DDC THIS MORNING...WITH A WEAK BOUNDARY EXTENDING NEWD FROM THIS SYSTEM INTO FAR SERN NEB AND THEN ESEWD ACROSS NRN MO. AS THIS SURFACE LOW SHIFTS SLOWLY NWD THIS AFTERNOON...A HOT AND VERY MOIST AIR MASS WILL GRADUALLY SPREAD NWD. MORNING ANALYSIS ALREADY INDICATES MLCAPES NEAR 3000 J/KG AND WITH ADDITIONAL WARMING...SHOULD BE AOA 4000 J/KG ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE BOUNDARY. ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS WERE OCCURRING THIS MORNING IN NEB...WITHIN AREA OF LOW LEVEL WARM ADVECTION. IN TIME...THESE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO BECOME SURFACE BASED...WITH MORE STORMS LIKELY TO DEVELOP IN EXTREME NERN CO/WRN NEB AS LARGE SCALE LIFTING SHIFTS IN FROM THE WEST. ONCE SURFACE BASED STORMS DEVELOP...THE COMBINATION OF EXTREME INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE SHEAR AT 40-50 KT WILL LIKELY RESULT IN INTENSE SUPERCELLS WITH VERY LARGE HAIL. ALSO...SURFACE LOW OVER WRN KS SHOULD BACK LOW LEVEL WINDS AND STRONGLY VEERING WINDS IN THE BOUNDARY LAYER WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR A FEW TORNADOES. BY EARLY EVENING...THESE STORMS ARE LIKELY TO C

sections.title: SRN MN/NORTHERN IA
sections.text: WV IMAGERY INDICATES A REMNANT UPPER LOW WAS LOCATED OVER WRN MN AND WAS MOVING SLOWLY NEWD. AT THE SURFACE A WEAK FRONT/TROUGH STRETCHED FROM NRN IA NWWD ALONG THE ND/MN BORDER. ALTHOUGH INSTABILITY WILL NOT BE PARTICULARLY STRONG...MLCAPES AOB 1000 J/KG...STRONGLY VEERING AND STRENGTHENING WINDS WITH HEIGHT WILL RESULT IN CONSIDERABLE VERTICAL SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS. AMBIENT LOW LEVEL VORTICITY AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL SUPPORT ISOLATED TORNADOES...ALONG WITH HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. THE STORMS SHOULD WEAKEN SHORTLY AFTER SUNSET WITH LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING.

sections.title: SERN OH/SWRN PA/WV
sections.text: AT LATE MORNING...A WEAK SURFACE LOW WAS LOCATED IN NRN OH...WITH A WARM FRONT EXTENDING SEWD ACROSS ERN OH/WV. A WEAK COLD FRONT STRETCHED FROM THE SURFACE LOW WWD ACROSS NRN IN/IL WITH A LARGE WARM SECTOR SOUTH AND WEST OF THE PREVIOUSLY MENTIONED FRONT. STORMS ARE MOST LIKELY ALONG AND EAST OF THE FRONT WHERE LOW LEVEL FORCING WILL BE THE GREATEST...THOUGH EXTENSIVE CLOUDS AND COOL SURFACE TEMPERATURES SHOULD TEMPER THE THREAT EAST OF THE WARM FRONT. STORM INITIATION AND EVOLUTION IN THE WARM SECTOR IS MORE UNCERTAIN AS DUE TO CONSIDERABLE CLOUDS AND WHAT APPEARS TO BE WEAK CONVERGENCE. HOWEVER...IF STORMS DO DEVELOP NEAR THE FRONT... SUFFICIENT SHEAR AND INSTABILITY WILL EXIST FOR A FEW SUPERCELLS WITH A TORNADO OR TWO POSSIBLE.

sections.title: TN/KY SEWD INTO THE SERN STATES
sections.text: NORTHWEST MID LEVEL WINDS AT 30-40 KT SHOULD PERSIST ACROSS THE REGION THROUGH THE PERIOD. AT THE SURFACE...A BACK DOOR QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT STRETCHED FROM NEAR THE SC/GA BORDER NWWD INTO THE SRN APPALACHIANS. ELEVATED CONVECTION HAS BEEN OCCURRING OVER TN/KY...BUT HAVE SO FAR THE ACTIVITY HAS BEEN WEAK. WITH HEATING THE TN STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO INTENSIFY AND OTHER STORMS ARE LIKELY TO DEVELOP/INTENSIFY IN AREA WHERE STRONG DIFFERENTIAL HEATING OCCURS. MODERATE INSTABILITY AND 30-40 KT DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL SUPPORT A DAMAGING WIND/HAIL THREAT INTO THE EVENING HOURS.

sections.title: ERN NM/WRN TX/SWRN KS
sections.text: TEMPERATURES NEAR 100 DEGREES ARE EXPECTED LATE THIS AFTERNOON OVER PORTIONS OF WRN TX/FAR ERN NM. VISIBLE AND WV IMAGERY SHOWS MID/HIGH LEVEL MOISTURE STREAMING NWD FROM MEXICO INTO THIS REGION...WITH A POSSIBLE MCV ABOUT 30 SE CNM. STRONG HEATING COMBINED WITH WEAK DRYLINE CONVERGENCE AND LIFT ASSOCIATED WITH MCV SHOULD AID IN HIGH BASED STORMS THIS AFTERNOON. LARGE TEMPERATURE/DEWPOINT SPREADS WOULD FAVOR STRONG WIND GUSTS WITH THE HEAVIER RAIN CORES. ..IMY/HURLBUT.. 06/17/2009

sections.title: NERN CO EWD INTO NEB/NRN KS/IA/MO
sections.text: NO APPRECIABLE CHANGE TO MDT RISK AREA/FCST. EXTENDED SLGT RISK/SVR PROBABILITIES WWD TO INCLUDE CO FRONT RANGE/PLNS. WEAK IMPULSE EDGING EWD ACROSS CNTRL NEB COMBINED WITH STRONG HEATING AND ENHANCED LLVL CONVERGENCE ALONG A RETREATING WRMFNT WERE IMPETUS FOR TSTM INITIATION ALONG NEB/KS BORDER EARLIER. LTH PROFILER EXHIBITED 45 KTS OF BULK SHEAR AND MAGNITUDE OF LAPSE RATES/BUOYANCY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS. INITIAL STORMS WILL TRACK ESE ALONG EDGE OF CAP INTO NRN MO WITH THREATS FOR VERY LARGE HAIL...DMGG WINDS AND A FEW TORNADOES. MEANWHILE...STRONGER IMPULSE EJECTING OUT OF THE FOUR-CORNERS REGION WILL TRANSLATE INTO THE CNTRL HIGH PLNS THIS EVENING. HIGH-BASED CONVECTION DVLPG OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN/INVOF BOUNDARIES OVER THE FRONT RANGE OF CO WILL ERUPT INTO NUMEROUS TSTMS BY LATE AFTN WITH SUPERCELLS LIKELY. ACTIVITY WILL ALSO DEVELOP FARTHER E ALONG/N OF THE WRMFNT INTO CNTRL/SRN NEB DURING THE EARLY EVENING. VERY LARGE HAIL...DMGG WIND GUSTS...A FEW TORNADOES CAN BE EXPECTED WITH INITIAL STORMS. ACTIVITY SHOULD GROW INTO AN MCS OVER CNTRL NEB LATE EVENING...THEN MOVE/DEVELOP EWD ACROSS IA AND NRN MO OVERNIGHT WITH HIGH WINDS/HAIL.

sections.title: W TX INTO CNTRL KS
sections.text: EXTENDED LOW SVR PROBABILITIES NWD INTO CNTRL KS. SUBTROPICAL IMPULSES MOVG NWD ALONG WRN PERIPHERY OF UPR RIDGE/WRN EDGE OF DEEP BOUNDARY LAYER MSTR HAVE ENHANCED HIGH-BASED TSTMS OVER W TX THIS AFTN. ACTIVITY SHOULD DEVELOP NEWD ALONG A DRYLINE FEATURE INTO SCNTRL/CNTRL KS BY THIS EVENING. INVERTED-V SOUNDINGS/HOT BOUNDARY LAYER WILL CONTRIBUTE TO ISOLD DMGG WIND GUSTS. /JPR ..JPR.. 06/17/2009 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1131 AM CDT WED JUN 17 2009/ AN ACTIVE CONVECTIVE DAY IS ANTICIPATED THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING FROM THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND MID/UPPER MS VALLEY REGION SEWD THROUGH THE TN/OH VALLEYS AND INTO THE SERN STATES.

sections.title: CNTRL PLAINS THROUGH MID AND UPPER MS VALLEY AREA
sections.text: EARLY THIS EVENING A WARM FRONT EXTENDS FROM E-CNTRL SD THROUGH SRN MN...NERN IA AND NRN IL. SECONDARY QUASISTATIONARY/WARM FRONT EXISTS FARTHER SOUTH FROM NRN KS EWD THROUGH N-CNTRL MO. DRYLINE/TROUGH STRETCHES FROM WRN TX NWD THROUGH SWRN KS. A RESERVOIR OF STRONG INSTABILITY EXISTS GENERALLY ALONG AND NORTH OF SRN MOST WARM FRONT FROM SRN NEB ESEWD THROUGH NERN KS AND CNTRL MO AS WELL AS ACROSS IA INTO SRN MN. THIS VERY UNSTABLE ATMOSPHERE WAS SAMPLED BY THE 00Z TOP SOUNDING THAT INDICATES SURFACE TEMPERATURES AROUND 90 WITH A WELL MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER /74F DEWPOINTS/ BENEATH 7.5 C/KM MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES RESULTING IN 5000-6000 J/KG MLCAPE. STORMS INCLUDING DISCRETE SUPERCELLS ARE EXPECTED TO CONTINUE DEVELOPING ACROSS NEB...IA...SRN SD AND SRN MN INTO MO THROUGH THE EVENING MAINLY ALONG AND NORTH OF WARM FRONT AS THE SLY LOW LEVEL JET STRENGTHENS AND AUGMENTS ISENTROPIC LIFT AND WARM ADVECTION. STORM DEVELOPMENT WILL ALSO BE AIDED BY MID LEVEL ASCENT RESULTING FROM IMPULSES EJECTING NEWD INTO THE PLAINS FROM TROUGH OVER THE WRN STATES. THIS REGION WILL REMAIN WITHIN BELT OF 40-50 KT MID LEVEL FLOW THAT IS RESULTING IN BULK SHEAR MORE THAN ADEQUATE FOR SUPERCELLS AND OTHER ORGA

sections.title: UPPER OH VALLEY
sections.text: A COLD FRONT STRETCHES FROM N CNTRL OH SWWD THROUGH SRN IND WITH A PRE-FRONTAL CONVERGENCE BOUNDARY FROM ERN OH SWWD THROUGH SWRN KY. SCATTERED STORMS INCLUDING A FEW SUPERCELLS ARE DEVELOPING ALONG AND EAST OF THESE BOUNDARIES WITHIN A ZONE OF DEEP ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING EWD THROUGH THE GREAT LAKES AND UPPER OH VALLEY. THE ATMOSPHERE IS MODERATELY UNSTABLE IN THIS REGION WITH BULK SHEAR OF 40-50 KT FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS. ISOLATED TORNADOES WILL ALSO REMAIN POSSIBLE NEXT FEW HOURS GIVEN STORM RELATIVE HELICITY OF 200-300 M2/S2 ALONG LOW LEVEL JET AXIS.

sections.title: TN VALLEY
sections.text: STORMS WILL LIKELY CONTINUE DEVELOPING NEXT FEW HOURS WITHIN NWLY FLOW REGIME WHERE 00Z RAOB DATA FROM NASHVILLE INDICATES STRONG INSTABILITY /3000+ MLCAPE/ AND UNIDIRECTIONAL BULK SHEAR OF AROUND 35 KT. SUPERCELLS ALONG WITH CLUSTERS OR BOWING SEGMENTS WILL REMAIN PROBABLE WITH ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL THE MAIN THREATS...THROUGH A TORNADO OR TWO CANNOT BE RULED OUT. ..DIAL.. 06/18/2009
